      Case Types: Complexity, Service Rate, Throughput & Time to Disposal

      Each bubble is a case type at this court. Position shows mean complexity and service rate. Bubble size shows throughput. Colour shows observed mean time to disposal.

      Case types · select any number

      Fitted duration levels: 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 2.5 years, 3 years and 5 years. Month/year labels use 21 working days per month.

      More frequent hearings ↑ ↓ Less frequent hearings
      ← Fewer hearings per case More hearings per case →

      ✓ Key takeaways

        Mean time to disposal (working days)

        Cooler colours = shorter disposal time; warmer colours = longer disposal time.

        Throughput H (hearings / working day)

        Bubble area is proportional to mean throughput. Zero throughput has zero area.

        How to read this plot

        1. Position: each bubble sits at its mean hearings per case (complexity, X) and mean hearings per case-month (service rate, S).
        2. Bubble size: larger bubbles mean more hearings are held per working day for that case type (throughput).
        3. Colour: warmer colours mean a longer observed mean time to disposal.
        4. Optional contours: dashed curves show fitted equal-disposal levels for 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 2.5 years, 3 years and 5 years. Disposal time is fitted with a case-count-weighted Gaussian smoother. Each type's weight is its disposed-case count multiplied by a Gaussian function of distance; smoothing width is 16% of the observed coordinate range, with a minimum of 2.5% of the chart axis range. Duration labels use 21 working days per month.

        Source: district court case records • monthly rates are adjusted for court working days
